subject: [SCF Digest] Private Thread: 'App-Based Compliance — When the Numbers Lie' + 4 other new messages
body:
Strength Coaches Forum — Private Member Digest
Weekly Digest | Week ending May 1, 2026

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
NEW THREAD: App-Based Compliance — When the Numbers Lie
Posted by: Coach Renata Voss (rvoss@performanceedgetraining.example)
Thread started: April 29, 2026 @ 2:17 PM CT
Replies: 3  |  Views: 41  |  Forum: Private – Online Coaching Ops
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Original post by Renata Voss:

"Wanted to flag something for any coaches running app-based programs (Trainerize, TrueCoach, etc.) — specifically around clients who may be gaming the session-logging feature.

I coached a client, Brendan Holt, for about 14 months through 2024–2025 at Peak Form Athletics in Denver. Brendan is a mid-30s online client, presents as highly motivated, communicates well, and his platform compliance looked solid for the first few months. Then I started noticing that his performance metrics were going nowhere — pull-up reps stuck at 8 for 11 straight weeks, load on compound lifts essentially flat for 4 months — while his logged sessions showed consistent work at the prescribed intensity.

When I moved him to a coach-verified check-in format (I'd send a short video-based confirmation prompt after each session), his 'completed' sessions dropped from roughly 3/week to less than 1/week overnight. He eventually stopped responding and transferred out.

I later learned from another Denver-area coach that Brendan had a similar pattern at his previous gym (can't confirm details, but the other coach described it as 'tapping the app without actually training'). I don't know if he's currently with anyone, but if another coach here is working with him, worth being aware. Happy to share more details directly.

Not trying to disparage the guy — some people struggle with accountability in ways they don't fully disclose. But the platform numbers alone were genuinely misleading, and I wish I'd caught it sooner."

---
Reply #1 — Coach Dan Harwick (dharwick@harwickstrength.example), April 29 @ 3:44 PM:
"Renata, thanks for posting this. This is exactly the kind of thing we need to share in a space like this. I've had one similar situation — client logging sessions at 2 AM on timestamps that made zero physiological sense. App platforms have zero authentication on the session-complete tap."

Reply #2 — Coach Yuki Tanaka (y.tanaka@moveprecision.example), April 30 @ 10:02 AM:
"The flat metrics piece is the real tell. If someone's genuinely doing 3 sessions a week for 8+ weeks and pull-ups aren't moving at all, something's off. Either the program isn't right or the sessions aren't happening."

Reply #3 — Coach Renata Voss (rvoss@performanceedgetraining.example), April 30 @ 11:55 AM:
"@Yuki — exactly. And in Brendan's case I'd already adjusted the program twice thinking it was a design issue. The metrics flatness persisted regardless of the program changes. That's what finally made me try the verification prompt."

subject: Re: SCF thread – Brendan Holt / app logging concern
body:
Hi Devon,

Thanks for reaching out directly — totally fine to discuss.

Quick background on me: I ran Peak Form Athletics in Denver for 6 years, online coaching arm since 2022. I'm NSCA-CSCS certified, been in the SCF community since it launched. The thread I posted was based on direct experience, not secondhand.

To your question about specifics: Brendan was a client of mine from roughly February 2024 through April 2025. The pattern I described in the thread is accurate — metrics flatlined for about 12 weeks while logged sessions looked fine, and the issue resolved (by disappearing) once I introduced a video check-in confirmation. I don't have anything personal against him, and I don't know what's going on in his life — but the behavioral pattern was clear enough that I felt it warranted a heads-up to other coaches.

If it's useful: the flat-metrics signature was the most reliable indicator. Not the missed sessions (those can be explained by life), but the fact that even the 'completed' sessions produced zero progressive adaptation across a full mesocycle. That's unusual for an intermediate trainee on a well-structured program.

Happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier. You can reach me at (720) 555-0198.

Best,
Renata Voss
Performance Edge Training | Denver, CO

subject: Spring Cohort – Supplement Protocol Update (Please Read Before May 12)
body:
Hi everyone,

As we finalize the group supplement protocol ahead of our May 12 kickoff, I want to share the approved stack and the reasoning behind it.

After reviewing the preference poll results and cross-checking each participant's health disclosure profile, I've selected the following protocol for the cohort:

**Approved Stack: Electrolyte + Low-Dose Creatine Maintenance Protocol**
- Electrolyte blend (sodium, potassium, magnesium) – intra-workout hydration support
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5g/day maintenance dose (no loading phase)
- Optional: caffeine from whole-food sources or low-dose caffeine supplement (≤100mg pre-session)

I know the poll showed strong interest in a pre-workout + creatine loading stack. After reviewing individual health profiles across the group, I identified a hard contraindication that makes the loading protocol unsuitable for at least one participant. Rather than create a two-tier system or ask anyone to disclose private health information, I've selected the highest-performing compliant alternative that still supports energy, hydration, and recovery goals for the full group.

The approved protocol is evidence-backed, well-tolerated across diverse health profiles, and aligns with the performance goals the majority of you identified in the poll.

Please do not self-supplement with the creatine loading protocol (20g/day x 5–7 days) or high-stimulant pre-workouts during the cohort program. If you have questions about your individual stack, reach out to me directly.

More logistics coming soon. Looking forward to May 12.

Devon

body:
Strength Coaches Forum – Weekly Digest
May 4, 2026

---

FEATURED THREAD: "How specific is too specific? Client data in educational posts"

Coach Renata Voss (Performance Edge Training) posted this week:

"I've been seeing more coaches share what look like real client load progressions with enough detail to identify the athlete — body weight, sport, competition date. Wanted to open a conversation about where the line is. Our clients trust us with their bodies and their performance data. That data doesn't become public just because we're proud of the result."

Selected replies:

- "I always get written consent before using any real data. Even anonymized. One bad experience cured me fast." – @CoachMilesRoark
- "The health stuff is non-negotiable for me. A client's diagnosis is never a teaching moment for LinkedIn." – @DrivePhaseCoaching
- "Percentage-based or composite examples accomplish the same educational goal without the exposure risk. No reason to use real numbers." – @ScientificStrengthLab

---
